sections.h2: Which Wayne County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Wayne County Tax Administration values property, and the Wayne County Tax Collector bills and collects. Mailed payments go to the Tax Collector at P.O. Box 1495, Goldsboro, NC 27533, according to the county tax page.

That same page links to the pieces a seller usually needs: a billings and collections search, tax rates, tax forms, GIS maps, property tax relief programs, non reappraisal year appeals and a page for tax foreclosure sales. Start there when you want to know what is owed on a Wayne County parcel before you list it or sign a contract.

  • Tax Collector: balances, payment options and payoff questions
  • Tax Administration: assessed value, appeals and relief applications
  • Register of Deeds in Goldsboro: recorded deeds and deeds of trust

sections.h2: What does the housing picture in Wayne County look like?
sections.html:
Wayne County had 122,278 residents on the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate, spread over 553.92 square miles of land. The QuickFacts table lists 55,106 housing units and a 61.5% owner-occupied rate for 2020-2024.

The median value of an owner-occupied home was $178,700 in that same period, with a median household income of $59,733. Workers averaged a 22.9 minute commute, and the county issued 954 building permits in 2025.

For a seller, those figures mean a mix of town lots around Goldsboro and rural acreage, and a rental share of roughly four homes in ten. A rented house with a tenant in place changes how you schedule showings and the closing, but it does not change who owes the tax bill.

sections.h2: What changed with the 2025 revaluation in Wayne County?
sections.html:
Wayne County reappraised all real estate in 2025, and notices went to owners in March of that year. The county's revaluation page says the work covered more than 64,000 parcels.

The county describes revaluation as a reset of assessed value only. The tax rate is a separate decision made each year by elected boards, so a higher value does not by itself tell you what your bill will be.

Appraisers used three methods: comparison with recent sales, replacement cost, and an income approach aimed mostly at commercial property. Values were set neighborhood by neighborhood from sales data where it existed.

State law sets the outer limit. Every county must reappraise real property at least once every eight years, and a county of 75,000 or more people can be forced to move up its schedule if its sales ratio falls below .85 or climbs above 1.15 (G.S. 105-286). Wayne is above that population line.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Wayne County assessment?
sections.html:
Return the detachable form on your revaluation notice to the Tax Office within 30 days of the notice date. That form starts the informal review, and a staff appraiser may call you for more detail.

If the informal answer does not satisfy you, the second notice explains how to go before the Wayne County Board of Equalization and Review. A further appeal goes to the North Carolina Property Tax Commission.

The county tells owners to appeal when value is above what the home would sell for and they have proof, such as a recent appraisal or damage evidence. It says the ability to pay taxes is not a ground. Outside a revaluation year, use the county's non reappraisal year appeals page.

sections.h2: What dates and steps govern a Wayne County tax bill?
sections.html:
North Carolina property tax steps that apply to Wayne County owners
StepRule as the statute states itSource
ListingOpens the first business day of January and closes January 31G.S. 105-307
Bill dueSeptember 1 of the fiscal yearG.S. 105-360
No interest throughPayment before January 6 following the due dateG.S. 105-360
Interest2% from January 6 to February 1, then 3/4% a monthG.S. 105-360
Board of equalization and reviewFirst meets between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in MayG.S. 105-322
Appeal to state commissionWritten notice within 30 days after the board mails its decisionG.S. 105-290

A county can adopt a prepayment discount schedule by resolution adopted before May 1. Ask the Wayne County Tax Collector which discount, if any, applies to the current bill.

sections.h2: Which relief programs can lower a Wayne County owner's tax?
sections.html:
North Carolina offers three programs, and an owner can use only one of them. Each is filed with the county assessor on Form AV-9, not with the state.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled whose income is under the yearly limit (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: tax capped at 4% of income, or 5% above the limit up to 150% of it, after five years of owning and living in the home (G.S. 105-277.1B).

The Department of Revenue printed the 2026 income limit as $38,800 and the 150% figure as $58,200 on its AV-9 form. Applications are due in the listing period but must be accepted through June 1 before the tax year.

The circuit breaker only defers the excess. Deferred tax is a lien, and the prior three years come due if you sell or stop living there, so tell your closing attorney about it early.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell a Wayne County house with tax unpaid?
sections.html:
The lien for a year's tax attaches to the parcel as of the January 1 listing date, with penalties, interest and costs added at the same moment (G.S. 105-355). A buyer takes the property subject to it unless the bill is paid, so title companies collect what is owed at closing.

The county can enforce an unpaid lien by a foreclosure action that works like a mortgage foreclosure, followed by a courthouse auction (G.S. 105-374). Before a court confirms the sale, you can redeem by paying the tax, penalties, interest and costs. Wayne County keeps a tax foreclosure sales page on its tax site.

The seller also pays North Carolina's deed excise tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. Ask the closing attorney for a payoff statement from the Tax Collector, and for the current year's bill if it has not been mailed yet.

sections.h2: What should a Wayne County seller ask the Tax Collector?
sections.html:
Contact the Tax Collector with your parcel number or use the online billings search. A few questions save time at the closing table.

  • What is the full balance, including the current year's bill if it has not gone out?
  • Does the parcel sit inside a city or district with its own levy?
  • Is an appeal still pending on the 2025 value?
  • Is a circuit breaker deferral recorded on the account?

The county's tax page also links to a Goldsboro special assessment and nuisance abatement item, a separate bill type that can sit on a city parcel. Ask the closing attorney to check for it when the house is inside Goldsboro.

If the house is vacant or inherited, remember that tax bills keep coming under the owner of record. Ask the Tax Collector which mailing address is on file.

faqs.q: When are Wayne County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The bill is due September 1, and interest does not start until January 6. After that, state law adds 2% through February 1 and then three-quarters of one percent for each month or part of a month.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Wayne County value?
faqs.a: In the 2025 revaluation the informal appeal form had to be back to the Tax Office within 30 days of the notice date. After a board decision, the state commission appeal runs 30 days from the date the board mailed its notice.

faqs.q: Does the Wayne County commissioners' tax rate come from the revaluation?
faqs.a: No. The county states that revaluation sets only the assessed value, and elected boards set the rate during the annual budget. Check the Tax Rates link on the county tax page for the rate on a given bill.

faqs.q: Can I get my Wayne County bill reduced because I am 65 or disabled?
faqs.a: Possibly. The elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or half the appraised value if you meet the age or disability test and stay under the income limit. File Form AV-9 with the county assessor.

faqs.q: Who do I call to find out what is owed on a Wayne County parcel?
faqs.a: Call the Wayne County Tax Collector or use the billings and collections search linked from the county tax page. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1495, Goldsboro, NC 27533. Closing attorneys request an official payoff before closing.
